title: Large & Emergency Vehicles, Buses, Trams
whatItIs: Large vehicles need more room and can't see you easily. Emergency vehicles need you to help them through safely.
keyFacts: Emergency vehicles with flashing blue, red or green lights, headlights or sirens: help them pass when it is safe.
Don't break the law to make way: no red lights, no bus lanes, no mounting the kerb.
Long vehicles may move out to the right before turning left: don't try to pass on their left.
If you can't see a lorry driver's mirrors, the driver can't see you.
Give way to buses signalling to pull out from a stop, when it is safe.

visual.caption: Sharing the road with big vehicles

items.title: Blue, red or green lights
items.text: Pull over to let them pass when it is safe and legal.

items.title: Long vehicles turning
items.text: They may swing out the other way first. Hold back.

items.title: Blind spots
items.text: Can't see the driver's mirrors? They can't see you.

items.title: Buses pulling out
items.text: Let them out of a stop when you safely can.

items.title: Trams
items.text: They can't steer round you and can be very quiet.

items.title: Stay back
items.text: Drop back so you can see past and the driver can see you.

a.label: Blue lights
points: Pull over when it is safe

b.label: Green lights
points: A doctor on an emergency call
Let them pass if you safely can

onTheTest.question: An ambulance with flashing blue lights is behind you at a red traffic light. What should you do?
options: Stay where you are, unless you can let it pass safely and legally
Move into the bus lane at once
Get out and wave it past
onTheTest.why: Help emergency vehicles through, but don't break the law or put anyone at risk. Don't go through a red light.

traps: Making way never means going through a red light or into a bus lane.
A long vehicle moving right may be about to turn left.
Can't see the lorry's mirrors? The driver can't see you.
